title: Which way does your bow lie?
hook: Which wrap pattern tends to hold better?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: Opposing knot stages make the balanced slipped reef bow sit across the shoe. The granny bow tends to turn along it; impact and moving lace ends can work a bow loose.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.
objective: Opposing knot stages make the balanced slipped reef bow sit across the shoe. The granny bow tends to turn along it; impact and moving lace ends can work a bow loose.

claims.text: Both illustrative loops start at 20 mm at step 0. Changing the second wrap changes its geometry and model loss rate without advancing steps. No empirical lifetime is claimed.

claims.text: Recall: Your first stage is left-over-right; the second is also left-over-right and the bow points along the shoe. Which change makes the stages oppose? Correct answer: Make the second stage right-over-left. Right-over-left opposes the left-over-right first stage, producing the balanced slipped reef bow in the stated schematic. The bow tends to sit across the shoe, but it can still fail. The drawing is not a tying tutorial.
